name: Shield Wall Warcry Titan
summary: Raises Shield Wall along fissures with Ahn's Citadel (guides also link the Kaom's Madness lineage support) and detonates the segments with Fortifying Cry and Infernal Cry for screen-wide physical explosions. Stone Skin, Hulking Form and Mysterious Lineage give it the biggest armour-and-life pool of any Warrior setup.
gear: One-handed mace plus the highest-armour shield you can find (Shield Wall damage scales from shield armour, not weapon damage); body armour with life, armour and 'armour also applies to elemental damage', capped resistances, attack-speed gloves, mana leech on a ring if mana is tight. Thrillsteel or Constricting Command helmets are optional upgrades.
strengths: Most-played Titan setup on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder
Huge armour + life pool; elemental hits mitigated by armour
Strong clear from chained wall detonations
weaknesses: Slow animations early in the campaign
Wall-then-cry rotation takes practice
Lower damage ceiling vs pinnacle bosses
Chaos damage is only covered by chaos resistance

name: Earthshatter Aftershock Titan
summary: Fast Earthshatter slams plant spikes that Titan-boosted Aftershocks (Earthbreaker, Ancestral Empowerment) detonate repeatedly, giving one-button clear and strong single target. Mysterious Lineage and Stone Skin keep it tanky; Sadist's Mercy adds Harbinger of Madness explosions.
gear: Sadist's Mercy one-handed mace with a high-armour shield (or a fast rare two-hander); stack attack speed, Aftershock chance and slam/melee skill levels, cap resistances and run The Brass Dome or a high-armour rare chest for Stone Skin.
strengths: One-button mapping and good boss damage
Armour + Stone Skin + extra life is a solid HC baseline
Second most common Titan skill on the HC ladder
weaknesses: Mana hungry; needs leech/regen
Needs attack-speed investment to feel good
Melee range against bosses
The Brass Dome was nerfed in 0.5.0 (500-600% armour)

name: Forge Hammer & Supercharged Slam Titan
summary: Two-handed mace slammer: Forge Hammer fissures clear packs and build rage, then Supercharged Slam and Hammer of the Gods delete bosses with Heavy Swing/Fist of War hits. Highest burst of the Titan options but commits you to long, unmodifiable attack animations.
gear: High physical-damage two-handed mace (Marohi Erqi is an optional unique), +melee/slam skill levels and Strength on jewellery; armour/life on every slot with capped resistances since there is no shield.
strengths: Huge single hits; best Titan bossing
Forge Hammer gives a safer ranged opener
Hulking Form boosts every small life/armour node
weaknesses: Supercharged Slam has a fixed attack time - getting caught mid-animation is a classic HC death
No shield block
Slower clear than Earthshatter
Needs careful positioning on bosses

name: Boneshatter Stun Titan
summary: Primes enemies for Heavy Stun with Leap Slam (Brink) and finishes them with Boneshatter shockwaves, using Hammer of the Gods and Earthshatter for bosses. Maxroll's budget Titan levelling route that carries comfortably into early and mid maps.
gear: Two-handed mace wielded in one hand via Giant's Blood plus a high-armour shield; upgrade the mace every ~10 levels (physical damage first) and socket Iron Runes, then add a dual-mace weapon swap and attack speed in maps.
strengths: Easy respec into Earthshatter or Shield Wall
weaknesses: Two-step prime-then-detonate gameplay
Over-levelled Leap Slam/cries drain mana
Endgame scaling below Earthshatter/Shield Wall
Never take Crushing Impacts (it removes priming)

name: Shield Wall Warcaller Warbringer
summary: Shield Wall fissures detonated by cooldown-free warcries (Warcaller's Bellow, which also explodes corpses), with Anvil's Weight and Imploding Impacts breaking armour below zero. Jade Heritage adds an on-demand Guard layer via Encase in Jade.
gear: One-handed mace + max-armour shield (weapon damage does not matter); body armour with life/armour and 'armour applies to elemental damage', capped resists, attack speed on gloves and skill speed on jewellery. Take Answered Call first in the campaign, then respec it into Warcaller's Bellow.
strengths: No warcry cooldowns - detonate walls freely
Armour broken below zero amplifies boss damage
Emergency Guard from Encase in Jade
weaknesses: Lower life/armour multipliers than Titan or Smith
Busy rotation (walls, cries, Sunder, Jade)
Slow early animations
Lower ceiling in very late endgame

name: Mortar Cannon Grenade Totem Warbringer
summary: Plants Mortar Cannon ballista totems that auto-fire Cluster Grenades from a crossbow while Answered Call summons Ancestral Spirits and Wooden Wall routes 20% of hit damage into the totems. Ranged, near one-button and the most-played Warbringer style.
gear: High physical-damage crossbow with the 'Grenade Skills fire an additional Projectile' implicit, ideally +ballista totem or +projectile skill levels; armour body with life and armour-applies-to-elemental, 35%+ movement speed boots. Fireflower amulet is an optional upgrade. Swap to the crossbow around level 52.
strengths: Fights from range behind totems and spirits
weaknesses: Clunky until the crossbow swap (~level 52) and ~level 70 scaling
Visual clutter can hide boss telegraphs
Damage and Wooden Wall protection drop if totems die
Needs a good crossbow base to scale

name: Firebringer Forge Hammer Warbringer
summary: Two-handed mace Warbringer that clears with Forge Hammer fire fissures and Stampede, then drops Shockwave Totems and Sunder for single target. Anvil's Weight and Imploding Impacts push armour break below zero while Answered Call/Wooden Wall totems absorb hits.
gear: High physical DPS two-handed mace (later dual-wielded via Giant's Blood); body armour with spirit for Herald/Banner plus armour and life; Strength and capped elemental resistances.
strengths: Totems tank and add single target
weaknesses: Many buttons (hammer, totems, Sunder, cries, banner)
Single target stalls when bosses move away from totems
No shield; lower defences than the Shield Wall variants
Few HC players to copy

name: Shield Wall Smith of Kitava
summary: Shield Wall and Resonating Shield detonated by Fortifying/Infernal Cry, worn over a Normal body armour that Smith's Masterwork enchants with extra life, armour against chaos, physical-taken-as-fire and ailment immunity. The most-played HC Smith and the most well-rounded Warrior defence.
gear: One-handed mace (Nebuloch optional) + highest-armour shield; a Normal (white) high-armour body armour is mandatory for Smith's Masterwork. Fire resistance also counts toward cold/lightning via Coal Stoker; armour and life everywhere else. Constricting Command is a popular helmet upgrade.
strengths: Armour applies to chaos and elemental damage
Coal Stoker makes resist capping easy
Most common Smith setup on the HC ladder; B-tier in 0.5.5 HC lists
weaknesses: Locked into a white body armour
Moderate damage ceiling
Rotation between walls and cries
Defences hinge on a high-armour chest base

name: Detonate Dead Forge Smith
summary: Heat of the Forge grants Fire Spell on Hit, which fills from Shield Wall and other hits and auto-casts Detonate Dead on corpses for chained screen-wide explosions. Sceptre + shield, with Coal Stoker and Forged in Flame raising every max resistance.
gear: Sceptre (for Spirit) + high-armour shield so shield skills do the hitting; Normal high-armour body armour for Smith's Masterwork; enough spirit for Fire Spell on Hit plus Purity/Herald. Constricting Command and The Brass Dome are common upgrades on the softcore ladder.
strengths: Best Smith map clear - corpses chain explosions
Max resistances raised via Forged in Flame
Most-played Smith build in softcore Forbidden Rites
weaknesses: Weak on bosses without corpses
Fire Spell on Hit energy interactions were bug-fixed in 0.5 - verify in game
Few HC players run it (less proven in HC)
Explosions are visually noisy

name: Balrog Fire Bear Smith
summary: Shapeshifts into a fire bear with the Fury of the King talisman: Walking Calamity rains meteors while Molten Crash and Maul hits proc Fire Spell on Hit and Cast on Elemental Ailment spells. Near-zero-button mapping with strong per-step life recovery.
gear: Fury of the King talisman (core, expensive), Normal high-spirit body armour for Smith's Masterwork, Goregirdle belt optional, amulet with +melee levels; cap resists and some chaos res. Two-handed mace on weapon swap for Forge Hammer bossing.
strengths: Big life recovery per step via Guts/Flare
Avatar of Fire + Smith fire nodes stack well
weaknesses: Needs Fury of the King to come online
Two buffs to maintain before fights
Cluttered visuals during spell cascades
0.5 changed trigger interactions (cries no longer proc Fire Spell on Hit directly)

name: Whirling Assault Smith of Kitava
summary: Quarterstaff Smith that spins through packs with Whirling Assault (Ancestral Call) and drops Tempest Bell on bosses, while hits fill Heat of the Forge's Fire Spell on Hit. Mobile and good at bosses, but without a shield it is the least forgiving Smith option.
gear: Rare quarterstaff with physical damage and attack speed (Collapsing Horizon for a crit/fire-spell variant), Normal body armour for Smith's Masterwork, attack speed gloves, capped resists. Constricting Command helmet is common.
strengths: Strong boss damage from Tempest Bell
Fire Spell on Hit adds free AoE
Smith defences without needing a shield
weaknesses: No shield block - least defensive Smith option
Subpar clear in heavily juiced maps
Combo/Tempest Bell timing to learn
Small HC sample size

name: Ice Shot Deadeye
summary: The dominant Ranger build of 0.5.x and by far the most-played Ranger on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder: Ice Shot and Tornado Shot freeze and shatter screens while Mirage Deadeye copies Ice Shot and frozen bosses eat Snipe. Freeze on everything is a defensive layer, backed by evasion, Wind Dancer and Ghost Dance energy shield.
gear: High physical-damage bow with crit and +projectile levels; Cadiro's Gambit quiver is the common upgrade. Hybrid evasion/energy shield armour, capped resistances, then crit and attack speed; many top HC players convert to Chaos Inoculation once ES is high.
strengths: Freezes nearly everything, so packs rarely get to attack
Proven on the HC ladder (most-played HC Ranger)
weaknesses: Snipe bossing needs you to stand still and channel
Evasion/ES can be chunked by unfreezable or damage-over-time sources
Low life pool until energy shield is built

name: Lightning Arrow Deadeye
summary: Lightning Arrow chains through packs while Herald of Thunder stacks extra coverage; plant Lightning Rods under bosses and fire Lightning Arrow into them for burst. Very fast mapping, but it relies on avoidance alone and has no freeze for crowd control.
gear: Bow with high physical and elemental damage plus crit; quiver with flat damage and +arrows. Life, evasion and capped resistances first, later hybrid evasion/energy shield; mana-on-kill jewels fix mana.
strengths: Among the fastest mappers in the game
Cheap, smooth league start (Lightning Rod + Lightning Arrow from Act 1)
weaknesses: No freeze; packs that survive can hit back
Mana problems until jewels/gear fix them
Rarely played on HC (almost no ladder proof)
Glass-cannon tendencies when crit gear is pushed

name: Twister Spear Deadeye
summary: Spear build that uses Whirling Slash to build whirlwinds and Twister to fling elemental tornados across the screen, with Barrage-boosted Twister bursts and Called Shots auto-applying Sniper's Mark for Frenzy Charges. Massive coverage and damage, but it's a squishy evasion build that leans on Dance with Death and cooldowns.
gear: Fast spear in weapon set 1 with an empty off-hand for Dance with Death, high-damage spear in set 2; The Taming ring is near-mandatory. Evasion body armour (Beastial Skin), pure energy shield helmet, life and resistances on everything else.
weaknesses: Squishy, especially early; avoidance-only defences
Vulnerable while waiting on cooldowns in boss fights
Weapon-swap and charge management are fiddly
Hardly any HC ladder presence

name: Glacial Lance Deadeye
summary: Throws Glacial Lance spears that explode into ice when you have Frenzy Charges, with a Mirage Deadeye copying every throw and full-screen freezes keeping you safe. Barrage and Called Shots + Sniper's Mark keep charges flowing for bossing.
gear: Crit spear (Akoyan base at endgame) plus a sceptre with Spirit for the many persistent buffs (Sacred Flame or Guiding Palm of the Eye are upgrades). Evasion/energy shield/deflection armour with a pure energy shield helmet for Subterfuge Mask; Valako's Roar charm helps charge generation.
strengths: Full-screen freezes are a strong defensive layer
Great clear and good boss damage
Several defensive layers (evasion, deflection, ES, Ghost Dance)
weaknesses: Campaign is rough without a budget unique enabler
Not built to face-tank bosses
Needs 240+ Spirit and charge upkeep; gear-hungry
Very little HC ladder presence

name: Ice Shot Pathfinder
summary: The same Ice Shot / Tornado Shot / Snipe bow kit as the Deadeye, but on Pathfinder for defence: Sustainable Practices turns about 30k evasion into roughly 60% elemental damage reduction, and Relentless Pursuit and Running Assault remove slows and heavy stuns while sprinting. This is the most common Pathfinder on the HC ladder and the top Pathfinder by level.
gear: Physical/crit bow and Cadiro's Gambit quiver, same as the Deadeye version. Stack evasion as high as possible (25-30k+), because Sustainable Practices converts it into elemental damage reduction; use hybrid evasion/ES armour and cap resistances.
strengths: Best elemental mitigation available to Ranger (evasion also reduces elemental damage)
Freeze crowd control plus immunity to slows and to heavy stun while sprinting
Top Pathfinder on the HC ladder
weaknesses: Less damage than Deadeye (no extra projectile or Point Blank)
Physical and chaos hits still only checked by evasion
Snipe bossing requires standing still

name: Poisonburst Arrow Pathfinder
summary: Chaos poison bow build: Poisonburst Arrow clears while Herald of Plague spreads poisons, and Gas Arrow, Vine Arrow and Toxic Growth stack poisons on bosses. Overwhelming Toxicity doubles the poison limit. This archetype holds the rank-1 HC SSF Pathfinder spot and has level-100 HC clears.
gear: High physical-damage bow (poison scales from hit damage); Plaguefinger gloves are the key upgrade and Voltaxic Rift is a common bow. Hybrid evasion/energy shield armour, capped resistances and chaos resistance, max life.
strengths: Ranged clear with Herald of Plague chain reactions
Poison ignores armour and stacks huge on bosses
Proven deep into HC (rank-1 HC SSF, level 100 HC)
Fastest movement of any Ranger setup
weaknesses: Damage over time ramps up slowly, so bursts are delayed
Mana management is tight early
Overwhelming Toxicity halves poison duration (nerfed in 0.5.0)
Wants Plaguefinger for full power

name: Gas Grenade Pathfinder
summary: Crossbow poison build: Gas Grenade drops growing poison clouds that persist (Persistent Ground III), Herald of Plague spreads poisons through packs and Explosive Shot detonates clouds for burst. No accuracy or precise aim needed, and you can play from well outside melee range.
gear: Crossbow with +projectile skill levels, flat elemental damage and crit (grenade damage/duration is a bonus); Plaguefinger gloves are core. Hybrid evasion/energy shield armour, 30%+ movement speed boots, capped resistances.
strengths: No accuracy or aiming required; clouds keep ticking while you reposition
Strong single target from stacked poisons plus Despair
weaknesses: Needs Persistent Ground III and Herald of Plague before clear feels smooth
Ramp-up time on bosses; pre-placing clouds matters
Reliant on Plaguefinger

name: Spark Comet Caster Pathfinder
summary: Caster Pathfinder that uses Path of the Sorceress to reach the Sorceress side of the tree: Spark clears, and Cast on Critical-triggered Comet plus Living Bomb handle bosses. Usually played as Chaos Inoculation with Eldritch Battery and an energy shield pool.
gear: Wand plus focus or sceptre with spell crit and +spell levels; Kalandra's Touch and Cloak of Defiance are common upgrades. Pure energy shield/evasion armour once Chaos Inoculation is taken; intelligence and mana scaling feed the build.
strengths: Very fast Spark clear with screen coverage
Big burst from Cast on Critical Comet
Relentless Pursuit/Running Assault make casting on the move smooth
weaknesses: Complex mana and energy setup (Eldritch Battery, Mana Remnants)
Chaos Inoculation means a respec transition and no life pool
Off-meta for Ranger, with very little HC ladder proof
Needs specific gear to come online

name: Ice Shot Amazon
summary: Crit bow Amazon that freezes and shatters packs with Ice Shot and Tornado Shot, then deletes frozen bosses with Snipe. The most-played Amazon on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder, using Stalking Panther for an evasion/energy-shield hybrid.
gear: High-accuracy physical bow with added cold (Penetrate wants 500+ weapon accuracy) plus a damage quiver; Energy Shield body armour with evasion helmet/gloves/boots for Stalking Panther, capped resistances and movement speed boots.
strengths: Ranged playstyle keeps you out of melee
weaknesses: Cannot face-tank; relies on evasion/deflection and freezing everything
Modest life pool (~1.6-2k) on HC ladder examples
Snipe timing on bosses takes practice
Freeze is weaker on pinnacle bosses

name: Bleed Rake Amazon
summary: Accuracy-stacking melee spear Amazon that dashes with Rake to stack huge bleeds, clears with Spearfield and Herald of Blood chain explosions, and finishes with Blood Hunt. Very high damage and mobility, but an evasion melee in one-life mode.
gear: High physical DPS spear with as much Accuracy as possible (Penetrate/Critical Strike scale off it); evasion/deflection armour, life and mana leech on rings, and a Stone Charm for stun.
strengths: Herald of Blood explosions chain through packs
weaknesses: Melee range evasion build: a few unlucky hits can kill in HC
Stun vulnerability early
Heavy attribute requirements
Few Amazons survive on the HC ladder (17 tracked)

name: Lightning Spear Amazon
summary: Classic crit 'Javazon': Lightning Spear for forking pack clear and Storm Lance plus Explosive Spear for bosses, layering evasion, Spectral Ward energy shield and Ghost Dance. Smooth mapper that gets outscaled at the very top end.
gear: High-accuracy, high-crit spear with +projectile skill levels and a buckler/off-hand; high-evasion body armour (~3k) for Spectral Ward, added attack damage on gloves/rings, mana leech.
strengths: Big ascendancy power spike once Critical Strike + Penetrate are online
weaknesses: Tough Act 1 and squishy early
Gear reliant (accuracy/crit on spear)
Bossing falls off at very high tiers
Mana-hungry without leech

name: Silverfist Companion Spirit Walker
summary: League-start companion build: tame the unique Mighty Silverfist in Act 3, then let it and the Wild Protector bear do the killing while The Catha's Balance adds your main-hand weapon damage to them. Very low budget and lets you stay out of harm's way.
gear: Crossbow/spear while levelling, then Tyranny's Grip (or a high-damage rare main hand for The Catha's Balance) with a sceptre for Spirit; stack +minion skill levels, life, capped resistances and movement speed.
strengths: Companion tanks and kills while you stay back
Few buttons, forgiving for new players
Works without mandatory uniques until maps
weaknesses: Must tame a specific unique beast (Mighty Silverfist, later Zekoa)
Acts 1-2 are played as a normal attack build before the swap
Damage depends on companion AI and survival
Idolatry lowers resistances per non-Idol augment

name: CI Beast Army Spirit Walker
summary: Endgame Sylvan's Effigy army: Zekoa plus Azmerian Wolf, Wolf Pack and several tamed beasts, scaled by The Catha's Balance and Idolatry, with the player converted to Chaos Inoculation energy shield. The most common and highest-level Huntress setup on the HC ladder.
gear: Sylvan's Effigy sceptre (multiple companions) with Tyranny's Grip or a big two-hand main hand for The Catha's Balance; ES/evasion armour (4-5k ES before going CI), +minion levels, Spirit, minion splash belt, Idols for Idolatry.
strengths: Dominant Huntress build in HC (most tracked level 98-100 Huntresses)
Chaos Inoculation plus a wall of companions makes you very hard to kill
Massive minion damage that scales with gear
weaknesses: Very expensive endgame (Sylvan's Effigy, runemastered weapon, Idols)
CI swap needs ~4-5k ES first; stun threshold must be fixed
Requires taming specific unique beasts
Many reservation/Spirit puzzles

name: Owl Twister Spirit Walker
summary: Whirling Slash builds whirlwinds that Twister consumes, with Ice-Tipped Arrows and Barrage adding elemental ground and projectiles for huge off-screen clear. Primal Bounty/The Mhacha's Gift empower attacks on dodge, while the Wild Protector bear absorbs hits.
gear: Fast attack-speed spear in set I for Whirling Slash/Barrage and a high flat-damage crit spear in set II for Twister; evasion/deflection on all armour, flat physical/cold on weapons, frenzy charge generation (Valako's Roar charm).
strengths: Strong single target once whirlwinds are stacked
Both main skills available at level 1; no uniques required to start
weaknesses: Combo setup (Whirling Slash x3 then Twister) leaves you exposed
Lower life pool than the companion builds
Damage drops if you leave the whirlwind area
Evasion-based: random big hits are a HC risk

name: Bleed Rake Ritualist
summary: Spear-and-shield bleed/poison Ritualist: Rake and Blood Hunt for bosses, Spearfield and Herald of Blood with Bursting Plague for chain explosions, Blood Boil for extra damage. The extra ring slot and Mystic Attunement fund resistances, leech and flat damage; the most common Ritualist on the HC ladder.
gear: High physical spear plus a block shield; three rings (Venopuncture plus flat-physical/leech rares) and an amulet boosted by Mystic Attunement; Ryslatha's Coil belt, evasion/deflection armour and capped resistances.
strengths: Shield block, leech and Wildwood Persistence give real sustain
Chain-explosion clear with Herald of Blood
Can kite with the DoT if needed
No entry cost for the core
weaknesses: Ritualist is gear-dependent; weak until the jewellery is good
Melee range on bosses
Mana management (Unfurled Finger path reduces mana)
Only ~30 Ritualists tracked on the HC ladder

name: Jewellery Twister Ritualist
summary: The Twister/Whirling Slash/Barrage spear engine played on Ritualist, trading Spirit Walker's companions for a third ring, 25% stronger rings and amulet and an extra charm slot. Big damage ceiling once jewellery is rich, but squishier than the Spirit Walker version.
gear: Same two-spear setup as Twister Spirit Walker (attack-speed spear in set I, flat-damage crit spear in set II); three rings and an amulet with flat elemental/physical damage and resistances; evasion/deflection armour.
strengths: Jewellery slot gives a high gear ceiling
Extra charm slot for ailment/stun protection
weaknesses: No bear tank or companions; squishier than Spirit Walker Twister
Back-loaded power, poor league start
Combo setup leaves you exposed
Rarely seen on the HC ladder (popular only in softcore)

name: Spark CI Ritualist
summary: Caster Ritualist with wand/focus or sceptre/focus spamming Spark, using Chaos Inoculation energy shield, Convalescence and three amplified rings. Popular in softcore; in hardcore it's mostly seen as a rarity/culling support setup, so the solo damage version needs dedicated damage jewellery.
gear: Wand or sceptre with a focus (+spell skill levels, crit); pure energy shield armour for CI, three rings and an amulet with ES, resistances and cast speed (Mystic Attunement amplifies them); Heart of the Well/Megalomaniac jewels at high budget.
strengths: Fully ranged and Chaos Inoculation makes chaos damage irrelevant
Mind Phylacteries lets mana fire charms
Strong ES pool with jewellery amplification
weaknesses: Most ladder versions are rarity/culling party builds, not solo damage
Spark single target is mediocre
CI needs a full ES gear swap; weak before that
Expensive jewellery-driven scaling

name: Permafrost Bolts Witchhunter
summary: Crossbow build that freezes packs with Permafrost Bolts and shatters them with Fragmentation Rounds, protected by an evasion-scaled Sorcery Ward barrier. Same skill from level 1 to endgame with no required uniques.
gear: Crossbow with high flat physical/cold and attack speed; evasion/life/resist armour (evasion scales the Sorcery Ward and Deflection), flat elemental attack damage on rings and gloves.
strengths: Sorcery Ward absorbs all hit types after Ceremonial Ablution
weaknesses: Obsessive Rituals halves armour/evasion: once the Ward breaks you are squishy
HC ladder median life only ~1,750
Positioning-sensitive (Fragmentation Rounds wants close range)
Freeze is weaker on pinnacle bosses

name: Grenadier Witchhunter
summary: Oil, Gas and Cluster Grenades clear packs while Explosive Grenade and Flash Grenade handle bosses, with Sorcery Ward as the main defensive layer. A cheap, fast league starter with a modest damage ceiling.
gear: Physical or fire crossbow (Bombard/Cannonade bases with grenade projectile mods); evasion + life + resists everywhere, movement speed boots, flat damage to attacks on rings/gloves.
strengths: Grenades fire from safety and over walls
Flash Grenade stuns and breaks armour
Sorcery Ward vs all hit types
weaknesses: Low damage ceiling
Grenade cooldown/fuse delays make clutch kills unreliable
Button-heavy boss rotation
Low life pool once Ward is down

name: Twister Spear Witchhunter
summary: Spear melee/projectile hybrid: Whirling Slash builds whirlwinds that Twister launches across the screen, using Weapon Master's extra weapon-set points and Dance with Death skill speed. Very fast mapping, gear-hungry.
gear: High physical/crit spear with +projectile levels, empty off hand for Dance with Death; evasion + life armour, attack speed and projectile levels on gloves.
strengths: Huge damage once The Taming is acquired
Weapon Master gives many extra points
weaknesses: Needs walls/terrain for best single target
High APM, multiple buttons
Gear-dependent (The Taming)
Low life once Ward is down

name: Galvanic Shards Stormblast Witchhunter
summary: Lightning crossbow build: Galvanic Shards chain through packs and Herald of Thunder spreads damage, while Stormblast Bolts detonated by Explosive Grenade delete bosses. High ceiling but investment-heavy and fragile.
gear: Crossbow with high physical damage and extra-bolt implicit; Hyrri's Ire and evasion gear to scale the Ward, Painter's Servant gloves for elemental damage, capped resists.
strengths: Stormblast detonation gives burst boss damage
weaknesses: Requires high investment to function
Lowest effective HP of the Witchhunter options (few HC players)
Sorcery Ward is the only big layer; life is low
Boss burst needs grenade timing

name: Supporting Fire Minion Tactician
summary: Unleash Hell! grants Supporting Fire, an artillery minion army that rains arrows over a huge radius while skeletons and Wolf Pack tank and add damage; A Solid Plan halves reservation for a big spirit pool. The dominant Tactician build on the hardcore ladder.
gear: Sceptre (+minion skill levels, spirit) with a shield; strength and armour/energy shield gear with life and resists, +minion levels on helmet/amulet, movement speed boots.
strengths: Scales offence and defence from Strength
No uniques required; great league starter
weaknesses: Bossing is merely OK
Minion stats compete for gear/suffixes
Must play crossbows until Supporting Fire comes online
Minion AI can lag on fast bosses

name: Galvanic Buff-Stacker Tactician
summary: Galvanic Shards and Herald of Thunder clear the screen while Stormblast Bolts handle bosses, with A Solid Plan funding Trinity, Berserk, Eternal Rage and other buffs, plus pinning enemies in place. Softcore powerhouse, rarely seen in hardcore.
gear: High physical crossbow with flat lightning; Painter's Servant to balance elements for Trinity, Alpha's Howl/Morior Invictus for spirit, hybrid armour/evasion with life.
strengths: Right Where We Want Them: pinned enemies cannot act
Very popular in softcore, well documented
weaknesses: Glass-cannon tendencies; very few HC players
Buff/reservation management is complex
Expensive uniques for full power
Relies on killing before being hit

name: Armour Grenadier Tactician
summary: Grenade crossbow build that pins enemies with Suppressing Fire and Right Where We Want Them while Iron Reflexes armour and Polish That Gear deflection soak hits. Maxroll's recommended way to level the Mercenary; a sturdy but modest endgame option.
gear: Bombard/Cannonade crossbow with grenade projectile mods and flat physical/fire; armour/evasion pieces (converted by Iron Reflexes) with life and resists, 30% movement speed boots.
strengths: Pin crowd control stops enemies acting
weaknesses: Lower endgame damage than minion/Galvanic Tactician
Grenade fuse/cooldown management
Almost no deep-endgame HC examples on the ladder
Armour is weak to big elemental hits

name: Flameblast Oil Grenade Gemling
summary: Channel Flameblast from a staff to ignite Oil Grenade ground, then spread the burning oil (and Tornado) across the screen from a crossbow weapon swap. By far the most-played and highest-levelled Mercenary build in hardcore.
gear: Fire/spell staff in weapon set I and a high-damage crossbow in set II; armour (via Iron Reflexes) with life and resists, gem quality via Gemcutter's Prisms (Advanced Thaumaturgy), movement speed boots.
strengths: Most-played and highest-level Mercenary on the HC ladder
Gem Studded red majority makes you immune to crit damage
weaknesses: Unusual weapon-swap playstyle takes practice
Channelling Flameblast roots you briefly
Screen effects can hurt FPS/visibility
Needs a power spike at level 52 (Flameblast)

name: Twister Spear Gemling
summary: Whirling Slash creates whirlwinds that Twister throws across the map, scaled by Advanced Thaumaturgy gem quality bonuses and Dance with Death. Extremely fast and high-damage with a large ES plus life pool on the ladder.
gear: Physical/crit spear with +projectile levels and an empty off hand; evasion/ES hybrid armour with life, projectile gem levels and attack speed on gloves, The Taming ring as the big upgrade.
weaknesses: More than one button, high APM
Single target suffers without walls
Melee range moments for Whirling Slash
Wants The Taming for full power

name: Grenadier Gemling
summary: Explosive, Cluster, Flash, Gas and Oil Grenades from a crossbow with Mortar Cannon support, using Gemling quality bonuses and Gem Studded crit immunity on a life/armour base. A sturdier, simpler grenade build than the Witchhunter version.
gear: Physical/fire crossbow with grenade projectile mods; armour (Iron Reflexes) + life + resists, flat damage to attacks on rings/gloves, gem quality for Advanced Thaumaturgy.
strengths: High life pool on the HC ladder (median ~2,750)
weaknesses: Grenade fuse and cooldowns delay damage
Several buttons for bosses
Armour alone struggles with big elemental hits
Less clear than Flameblast Gemling

name: Spark Comet Gemling
summary: Energy-shield spellcaster: Spark applies ailments and crits that trigger Comet and Arc, while Advanced Thaumaturgy boosts Spark's projectile count and Blink range. High effective HP but no avoidance and needs specific uniques.
gear: Wands/sceptre or focus with +spell levels; high energy shield, mana cost efficiency and cast speed on gear, resists capped with attribute suffixes.
strengths: Very high effective HP from ES
Strong at both mapping and bosses
weaknesses: No avoidance layer; pure EHP
Relies on Split Personality/Maligaro's Virtuosity
Screen clutter hurts visibility
Few HC players compared with Flameblast Gemling

name: Arc Stormweaver (CI Archmage)
summary: Chaining Arc fed by Orb of Storms Lightning Infusions, scaled through maximum mana with Archmage and Mana Tempest on a Chaos Inoculation energy shield pool. The most documented self-found friendly Stormweaver, with very fast clear and a smooth campaign.
gear: Voltaic/Chiming Staff early, then Wand + Focus with +levels to Lightning/Spell skills, spell damage and extra elemental damage; pure ES armour with Spirit on the body for Archmage, 20-35% movement speed boots.
strengths: Huge AoE clear from chaining Arc
Large ES pool after Chaos Inoculation
weaknesses: Don't-get-hit playstyle: no armour/evasion layer, so one-shots are the main HC risk
Overcharge reflects Shock back onto you
Mana and ES are tied together through Eldritch Battery
Must keep Orb of Storms infusions up for damage

name: Spark Trifusion Comet Stormweaver (Adonia's Ego)
summary: Crit Spark with Cast on Elemental Ailment Comet, Firestorm and Tempest Caller's Elemental Storm, cycling all three Infusions into Power Charges for Adonia's Ego's Pinnacle of Power. The dominant Stormweaver setup on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder, but gear-hungry and button-heavy.
gear: Adonia's Ego wand (grants Pinnacle of Power) with a Spirit sceptre (Sacred Flame is common) and Maligaro's Virtuosity; pure ES rares with resistances, then Heart of the Well/Prism of Belief jewels. Some players run Mind Over Matter instead of CI.
strengths: Top HC-ladder Stormweaver: very high damage
Excellent clear from Spark plus Comet triggers
Elemental Storm adds free boss damage on crit
weaknesses: Expensive: relies on Adonia's Ego and Maligaro's Virtuosity
High-APM rotation (infusions, charges, weapon swap); mistakes under pressure kill in HC
Struggles with ailment-threshold map mods
Glassy ES-only defence

name: Frostbolt Cast on Crit Comet Stormweaver
summary: Snakepit makes Frostbolt fork and explode, crits generate energy for Cast on Critical Comet, and Strike Twice plus Shaper of Storms let cold hits apply double shocks. Strong clear and bossing once Snakepit is found; levels as Ice Nova/Snap with Cast on Elemental Ailment.
gear: Attuned Wand + Sacred Focus with +levels to Cold/All Spell skills and spell crit; Snakepit in the left ring slot and Maligaro's Virtuosity gloves, then stack ES, mana and mana regeneration.
strengths: Cast on Critical Comet gives strong single target
Freeze plus double shock locks packs down
weaknesses: Snakepit is build-enabling; without it play the weaker Cast on Elemental Ailment Ice Nova variant
Mana sustain is the biggest problem in long boss fights
Rare on the HC ladder; ES-only defence with no stun answer beyond charms

name: Ice Nova Comet Chronomancer
summary: Crit Ice Nova clears while Cast on Critical (Cast on Elemental Ailment while leveling) fires Comet, with Frost Wall crystals for boss burst. Phased Form's 30% less damage taken plus Temporal Rift make it one of the safest self-cast Sorceress setups.
gear: Staff with +levels to Cold/All Spells, spell crit and extra fire/lightning damage; Spirit on body armour and amulet for Cast on Critical + Blasphemy; life, Runic Ward and ES on armour (~2k life / 1k ward / 1k ES), capped resistances.
strengths: Phased Form + Temporal Rift erase a large share of big hits
Budget-friendly: no mandatory uniques, CoA version league-starts
Temporal Chains/Apex slows make packs manageable
weaknesses: Infusion and wall management adds complexity
Phased Form's delayed 30% must be respected or cleared with Temporal Rift
Mana-hungry before sustain nodes and gear

name: Grim Pillars Spell Totem Chronomancer
summary: Spell Totems cast Grim Pillars (and Bitter Dead) for free, bypassing the Runic Ward cost, while Entangle with Biting Frost consumes the ice crystals for big hits. A proven HCSSF league starter (top-3 on day one of 0.5.5) that fights from behind totems and Time Freeze.
gear: Wand + Sceptre: wand with +levels to Cold/All Spell skills (Grim Pillars gem level matters hugely), high-Spirit sceptre and Spirit on amulet/body for 75-Spirit totem breakpoints; life + ES rares with capped resistances.
strengths: Totems deal the damage so you can stay at range
Time Freeze + Time Snap give two emergency 'stop the boss' buttons
weaknesses: Grim Pillars gem is hard to obtain in 0.5.5 (limited drop areas); level with chaos/lightning spells first
Weak until Grim Pillars and enough Spirit for totems
Totem placement slows mapping; heavy visual effects

name: Essence Drain Contagion Chronomancer
summary: Chaos damage over time: Contagion spreads, Essence Drain applies the big DoT, and Dark Effigy totems bombard everything afflicted, on a Chaos Inoculation ES base. Cheap and simple; Chronomancer adds Phased Form, Time Freeze and cooldown resets for safety.
gear: Wand + Focus with +levels to Chaos/All Spell skills and chaos/DoT damage; pure ES armour after Chaos Inoculation, capped elemental resistances.
strengths: Very cheap, works on self-found rares
Ranged DoT: never needs to stand in melee
Phased Form + Temporal Rift + Time Freeze layer well
weaknesses: Lower damage ceiling than cold crit builds; DoT ramp is slow on bosses
Few dedicated 0.5.x Chronomancer guides; setup based on HC ladder data and Witch Essence Drain guides
ES-only pool with modest stun protection

name: Fire & Sand Djinn Disciple
summary: Command Kelari (sand) and Ruzhan (fire) Djinn, boosted by Muster from a full skeleton/wolf army, while The Fourth Teaching and Sacred Rituals turn a big ES pool into armour. The most-played and safest Sorceress on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder.
gear: Sceptre + Focus (or Shield) with +levels to Minion skills and Spirit; +minion levels on helmet/amulet, pure ES armour after Chaos Inoculation (5-6k ES), Enfolding Dawn and Bones of Ullr for Spirit/reservation.
strengths: Most-played HC Sorceress (about 18% of all HC Forbidden Rites characters are Disciples)
Invulnerable Djinn plus a minion meat shield
ES-to-armour (Sacred Rituals) and faster ES recharge
weaknesses: Button-heavy command rotation
Minion clutter hurts visual clarity; hidden ground effects are an HC danger
Peak damage needs runeforged uniques and minion gear

name: Navira's Fracturing Ice & Sand Djinn Disciple
summary: Ice Nova and chilled ground freeze packs so Navira's Fracturing shatters them, while Kelari handles single target and The Fourth Teaching/Sacred Rituals keep you tanky. Heavy crowd control makes it a very safe HC mapper.
gear: Sceptre + Focus: minion damage/crit and +minion levels on weapon set 1, cold/spell crit and cast speed on set 2; armour/ES hybrid or pure ES with capped resistances.
strengths: Freeze, chill and slows keep enemies almost permanently controlled
Very common on the HC ladder (about 300 characters)
weaknesses: Damage harder to scale than the fire Djinn version
Freeze-resistant bosses blunt the crowd control
Many active buttons

name: Frostbolt Cast on Crit Comet Disciple
summary: Self-cast Snakepit Frostbolt that triggers Comet on crit, using Instruments of Power to wield a staff and focus together and Baryanic Leylines to boost Time-Lost jewels. Disciple's ES-recharge and ES-as-armour nodes make it notably tankier than the Stormweaver version.
gear: Staff + Focus (Instruments of Power) with +levels to Cold/All Spells and spell crit; Snakepit left ring, Maligaro's Virtuosity, Time-Lost Sapphires; increased ES recharge on all armour pieces.
strengths: High single target via Frost Wall crystals + Comet
ES recharge and ES-as-armour defences from Disciple
weaknesses: Needs Snakepit and ~70% crit before the Cast on Critical swap
Weak Frostbolt during early campaign (level with Ice Nova)
Relies on Infusion Remnants for consistent leveling damage

name: Minion Army Infernalist
summary: Spectre-led minion army (Vaal Guard spectres, Skeletal Reavers, Storm/Frost Mages, Brutes) buffed by Pain Offering, with Loyal Hellhound and Beidat's Will for extra Spirit. The most-played Infernalist setup on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder; you stay back on an energy shield + life shell.
gear: Rattling or Stoic Sceptre plus an energy shield shield; +# to Level of all Minion Skills on sceptre, helmet and amulet, then Spirit; energy shield on armour pieces with 75% elemental and 60%+ chaos resistance. Bones of Ullr and Prism Guardian are the most common upgrades on the HC ladder.
strengths: Minions hold aggro so you play at range
Command skills (Intimidate, shock, frost shield) add flexible boss damage and defence
weaknesses: Vaal Guard spectres cause visual clutter and frame drops, which is dangerous in hardcore
Many buttons and spectre binding in the endgame
Your own defence is ES plus resistances only, so you die if the army collapses

name: Skeletal Sniper Infernalist
summary: Budget league starter where Skeletal Snipers shoot from range, Volcano ignites packs and Skeletal Reavers hold the front line. It uses the same Hellhound, Altered Flesh and Beidat's Will defensive core as the spectre army but doesn't need specific spectres.
gear: Sceptre with +minion skill levels, added physical damage and increased Spirit; energy shield bases everywhere, and later a belt with 'Minions' Strikes have Melee Splash'. Keep about 1400+ life under ES, 75% elemental and 60% chaos resistance.
strengths: Cheapest Witch starter, with no uniques required
weaknesses: Mana-hungry early, so it needs Arcane Surge/Efficiency
Lower ceiling than the spectre or Lich minion variants
Snipers are fragile, so Reavers and the Hound must hold aggro

name: Cast on Critical Comet Infernalist
summary: Crit caster that spams Frostbolt (Spark while levelling) to charge Cast on Critical, which auto-casts Comet. Pyromantic Pact removes mana management and Grinning Immolation adds 50% more crit damage, while recoup/ES (or armour stacking) offsets the self-damage.
gear: Wand + focus or staff with cast speed, spell levels and critical chance; energy shield bases with life/ES recoup; overcap fire resistance since Altered Flesh converts cold and lightning taken to fire. High-end variants armour-stack (The Brass Dome) or add ward.
strengths: Pyromantic Pact means no mana management
Smooth Spark to Frostbolt to CoC progression
weaknesses: Pyromantic Pact deals your max Life+ES as fire damage when Infernal Flame caps, so a misplay can kill in hardcore
Grinning Immolation ignites you on crits and needs recoup/regeneration to offset
CoC trigger rules are complex, and Comet stops if crit or energy is too low
Expensive to reach its final form

name: Demon Form Infernalist
summary: Shapeshifts into Demon Form and runs a lightning trigger package (Spark via Elemental Invocation, Ball Lightning via Cast on Critical, Lightning Warp), with Pyromantic Pact replacing mana. Sacrosanctum recoup keeps ES topped up, making it extremely fast and mobile but defensively demanding.
gear: Chiming Staff or Dueling Wand with spell levels and cast speed; Sacrosanctum body armour for elemental recoup; overcap elemental resistances by about 25%.
weaknesses: Lightning Warp can teleport you into danger
Recoup stops when you stop casting, so recovery is poor while kiting
Game8 explicitly does not recommend it for hardcore
Some map modifiers brick it

name: Essence Drain Contagion Lich
summary: Chaos damage-over-time caster: Contagion spreads Essence Drain through packs while Dark Effigy totems and Despair handle bosses. Eternal Life and Soulless Form on a large ES pool make it one of the safest self-cast Witch starters and the most-played Lich skill on the HC ladder.
gear: Wand + focus (or staff) with +levels to chaos/spell skills and cast speed; maximum energy shield on every slot, Atziri's Disdain helmet; cap elemental resistances and push chaos. A Snakepit ring adds a chain.
strengths: Large ES pool, and Eternal Life stops bleed/poison from touching your life
Cheap, fast campaign (maxroll quotes about 5 hours SSF)
weaknesses: DoT ramp-up means bosses take setup time
'Don't get hit' ES playstyle without an armour or evasion layer
Soulless Form/Atziri's Disdain bypass means some damage always reaches life

name: Minion Army Lich
summary: Large reviving army (Gargantuan Wasp spectres, Wolf Pack, Skeletal Clerics, Brutes and Storm Mages) empowered by Necromantic Conduit's Unholy Might. It sits behind the Lich's Eternal Life + Soulless Form energy-shield shell and is maxroll's tankiest minion option.
gear: Sceptre, helmet and amulet with +# to Level of all Minion Skills; energy shield on all armour, Spirit on body/amulet/sceptre; 75% elemental and 60%+ chaos resistance. Common upgrades are Bones of Ullr, Prism Guardian and Evergrasping Ring.
strengths: Very tanky from Eternal Life, Heavy Buffer and Wolf Pack/Loyalty damage reduction
Scales smoothly from campaign to endgame
weaknesses: Button-intensive early
Spectre visual clutter
Necromantic Conduit drains mana, so the buff drops when you go low on mana

name: Infernal Legion Companion Lich
summary: A tamed beast companion (Plague Harvester) linked to Infernal Legion II and Hulking Minions burns everything around it while you stack 10k+ energy shield, Ghost Dance and Temporal Chains, for near zero-button play. It swaps to Chaos Inoculation once ES reaches about 6k.
gear: Sceptre (Shrine early, then Stoic) with +minion levels; energy shield/evasion armour, about 6k ES before swapping to Chaos Inoculation and 10k+ in the endgame; cap the companion's fire resistance because Infernal Legion burns it.
strengths: Excellent defensive scaling from ES, Ghost Dance and Temporal Chains
weaknesses: Needs a specific captured rare beast (Plague Harvester with extra fire)
Forced close-range positioning
Not screen-wide AoE, and you have no damage if the companion dies

name: Crit Spark Blood Mage
summary: Spams Spark at 100% crit (Sunder the Flesh raises base spell crit to 15%) so Choir of the Storm triggers Lightning Bolt and Cast on Critical fires Arc. Vitality Siphon leech and Life Remnants sustain a hybrid life/ES pool, and it is the most-played Blood Mage skill on the HC ladder.
gear: Staff (or wand + focus) with +lightning/spell skill levels, cast speed and crit; a Choir of the Storm amulet with a high Lightning Bolt level; hybrid life/ES armour (Crimson Power turns body armour ES into life) and capped resistances.
strengths: Leech and Life Remnants give constant sustain
weaknesses: Defensively thinner than Lich ES shells
Sanguimancy gives skills a life cost, so careless casting drains your pool
Needs about 100% crit before Choir/CoC carry damage

name: Impending Doom Blood Mage
summary: One-button curse build: Elemental Weakness with Spell Cascade, Impending Doom and Doedre's Undoing triggers Doom Blast and exploding Witchtoads, and Sunder the Flesh lets the triggered blasts crit. It defends with mana stacking via Mind Over Matter/Eldritch Battery plus Blasphemy Temporal Chains.
gear: Wand + focus/shield (Sunsplinter is common on the HC ladder) with +spell/curse levels and high support-gem levels, since Doom Blast scales with gem level; stack mana and ES for Mind Over Matter/Eldritch Battery.
strengths: True one-button clear and single target
Huge boss damage from crit Doom Blast
weaknesses: Very expensive to max (guides quote 1200-1400 div)
The mana-pool defence collapses when mana is drained
Depends on the Doedre's Undoing lineage support and curse-AoE tuning

name: Plasma Blast Crossbow Blood Mage
summary: Crossbow attacker: Galvanic Shards and Shockburst Rounds map, and a charged Plasma Blast deletes bosses. Blood Barbs lets elemental damage build Bleeding that becomes Aggravated on cursed targets, so cheap rares deal heavy damage.
gear: Crossbow with high physical damage and +attack skill levels (Greater Iron Runes); ES/evasion armour with capped elemental resistances and a Tacati soul core for chaos; Stone and Thawing charms against crowd control.
strengths: Strong on a small budget thanks to Blood Barbs
weaknesses: Positioning dependent, since Plasma Blast must be charged and aimed
A missed blast in a boss fight is punishing
Thin ES/evasion defences, and few HC players run it

name: Plants Abyssal Lich
summary: Entangle and Thrashing Vines plant spells, watered by Thunderstorm for Accelerated Growth/Overgrow explosions, with Bonestorm for bosses; Rupture the Flesh chain-explodes cursed enemies for physical damage. A permanent low-life lock (Eternal Life + Atziri's Disdain) on about 8.5k ES makes it one of the tankiest 0.5 builds.
gear: Staff, with a Chiming Staff on weapon set 2 for Thunderstorm/Sigil; ES body and boots with life and resistances; Atziri's Disdain helmet is mandatory for the low-life shell (Soul Tether belt temporarily to drop below 35% life); Nightscale gloves for mana; cast-speed rings.
strengths: Screen-wide clear, and Rupture the Flesh scales off monster life
Among the tankiest 0.5 builds at endgame
Entangle works from level 1 (level as a normal Lich)
weaknesses: The Abyssal Lich unlock requires beating the Vessel of Kulemak pinnacle, a real risk on a HC character
The low-life setup (Soul Tether/Lifetap trick) is unintuitive
Mana hungry, and min-maxing is expensive

name: Projectile Twister Abyssal Lich
summary: Spear attacker: Umbral Well turns Skeletal Snipers into Umbral Souls for huge projectile speed, Whirling Slash stacks empower Twister, and Barrage with Olroth's Conviction repeats it for bosses. It is extremely fast and runs on energy shield, later Chaos Inoculation.
gear: Spear with high physical damage (The Ordained on a budget, Sacred Flame sceptre for boss burst); The Taming ring; Spirit on body and amulet; ES + Runic Ward boots; swap to Chaos Inoculation at 5-7k ES.
strengths: Strong single target via Barrage + Olroth's Conviction
weaknesses: Pure ES with no evasion before CI, so one-shot risk in hardcore
Boss fights demand positioning outside your presence
Needs the Abyssal Lich (Kulemak) unlock and physical spear damage for Armour Break

name: Hollow Form Whirling Assault Martial Artist
summary: Channel Hollow Form with Whirling Assault socketed so astral images perform the full Whirling Assault sequence, fuelled by Power Charges from Lochtonial Caress (Stonefist), Rend and Killing Palm. The most-played Monk setup on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder, finishing on Chaos Inoculation with evasion, deflection and Ghost Dance.
gear: High physical-DPS quarterstaff (Duality is the usual starter) with Amor Mandragora in weapon set 2 for Rend; Lochtonial Caress gloves become Fists of Stone via Way of the Stonefist and supply Power Charges. Evasion/ES bases, deflection and capped resists, and only switch to Chaos Inoculation once Energy Shield is around 3,000+.
strengths: Most-played HC Monk build (~60% of HC Martial Artists)
Layered evasion, deflection, ES and Ghost Dance
weaknesses: Poor visual clarity from images
CI transition is a risky window: needs a big ES pool first and no life-costing flasks
Charge generation leans on Lochtonial Caress
Squishier campaign on Ice Strike until Whirling Assault at level 41

name: Hollow Form Shield Wall Martial Artist
summary: Mace-and-shield Martial Artist that channels Hollow Form with Sunder and Shield Wall socketed, so images raise walls and slam them apart, with Volcanic Fissure adding slow, maim and bleed. Built for HCSSF: block, deflection, evasion/ES, Magma Barrier, shield armour and Chaos Inoculation make it the tankiest Monk option.
gear: One-handed mace (Sadist's Mercy in the endgame variant) plus a high-armour/block shield; Lochtonial Caress gloves supply Power Charges, Amor Mandragora/Wanderlust are common later picks. Evasion/ES armour and runes in the Runic Meridians sockets for resists and attributes; attack speed is the best damage stat because images place and break walls faster.
strengths: Very tanky: block, deflection, ES, armour on shield, Magma Barrier, CI
Effectively one button once set up
weaknesses: Weak and button-heavy early on the quarterstaff kit until the Act 4 swap
Attribute balancing is awkward
Melee range
PoB doesn't model Hollow Form well, so damage is hard to evaluate

name: Falling Thunder Martial Artist
summary: Quarterstaff Power Charge build: generate charges with Whirling Assault (Ailith's Chimes), Mantra of Destruction and Stonefist gloves, then spend them on huge Falling Thunder hits. Martial Adept and Martial Master let Heralds and Charged Staff build Combo; endgame goes Chaos Inoculation.
gear: Crit quarterstaff with elemental damage and +melee levels (Sinister Quarterstaff base); Stonefist gloves rolled for extra damage as lightning/cold, crit and Onslaught. Hybrid evasion/ES bases with curse immunity; Prism of Belief (+Falling Thunder levels) is the big jewel upgrade.
weaknesses: Rough Act 1
Charge/Combo upkeep must be managed
Melee positioning required
Takes Hollow Focus Technique early and respecs it later
CI needs a solid ES pool first

name: Hollow Focus Storm Wave Martial Artist
summary: Hollow Focus bells and Shattering Palm chain-react with Herald of Ice armour explosions for fast mapping, while overlapping Storm Wave fissures handle single target. Way of the Mountain adds stun mitigation and freeze scaling on an evasion/deflection base.
gear: Physical quarterstaff with attack speed, crit damage and +melee levels (Duality is an upgradeable alternative); Stonefist gloves with melee levels and physical damage. Stack evasion and deflection, amulet with +3 melee skills, and Vestige of Darkness for its blind aura early in endgame.
strengths: Strong single target with overlapping fissures
weaknesses: Monk has a slow start (guide levels on Twister)
Single target needs precise fissure placement
Mana problems until Oisín's Oath
No CI or block: relies on evasion/deflection and killing first

name: Ice Strike Invoker
summary: Classic cold quarterstaff Invoker: Ice Strike and Shattering Palm clear with Herald of Ice explosions, Tempest Bell and Unbound Avatar burst bosses. Endgame Chaos Inoculation plus Meditate over-buffers Energy Shield for a very large effective pool.
gear: Quarterstaff with physical/elemental damage, crit and +melee levels; ES-heavy evasion/ES body armour (Lead me through Grace... converts it to Spirit). Stack Energy Shield toward CI and cap resistances.
strengths: Very large ES pool with Meditate late
Strong boss burst with Tempest Bell and Unbound Avatar
weaknesses: Melee struggles early; Acts 2-4 are difficulty spikes
Spirit-hungry
Invoker is rare on the HC ladder (well behind Martial Artist)

name: Whispering Ice Comet Invoker
summary: Staff caster Invoker: Icestorm (from The Whispering Ice) and Ice Nova crit constantly while Maligaro's Virtuosity guarantees crits, so Cast on Critical fires Comet nonstop. The Soul Springs Eternal powers the meta gem, and Chaos Inoculation plus Meditate gives a large ES pool.
gear: The Whispering Ice staff (needs level 75; look for +7 levels and low cast-speed penalty) and Maligaro's Virtuosity gloves are mandatory. High-ES body armour for Spirit via Lead me through Grace..., plus +spell levels, cast speed, mana and mana regen on the amulet and rings.
strengths: Scales from cheap to luxury budgets
Ranged with heavy chill and Hinder
weaknesses: Endgame starts at level 75 (guide levels on Ice Nova/Frost Bomb)
Needs two specific uniques
ES-only CI pool demands active dodging and flask/Meditate upkeep
Bad map mods: chilled ground, curses, ailment threshold

name: Poisonburst Arrow Acolyte of Chayula
summary: Bow poison Acolyte: Poisonburst Arrow, Toxic Growth and Vine Arrow stack poison, with purple Remnants from Waking Dream/Lucid Dreaming and Archon of Chayula adding chaos damage. The most popular Acolyte build overall, and the most common one on the HC ladder.
gear: Physical-damage bow with a quiver (Hysseg's Claw is a popular weapon-set swap); evasion/ES armour with deflection, capped elemental resists, and movement speed. Chayula's Gift handles chaos resistance.
strengths: Ranged: fight from a safe distance
weaknesses: Life-based with moderate EHP: relies on evasion/deflection and not getting hit
DoT ramp-up is slower on tanky bosses
Remnant pickup needs some movement

name: Spearfield Poison Acolyte of Chayula
summary: Splinter of Lorrata lets any number of poisons stack, so Spearfield and Entangle pile up poison and Plague Bearer detonates the incubated poison. Archon of Chayula and Rage handle the boss burst.
gear: Splinter of Lorrata spear is required; prioritise maximum ES, evasion, resistances, +Plague Bearer levels, Spirit and deflection. Optional Alpha's Howl, Original Sin and Prism of Belief later.
strengths: Chayula's Gift removes the need for CI
weaknesses: Slow movement while setting up poison
Damage can feel inconsistent
Build-enabling unique needed before it works
Small HC ladder presence

name: Minion Army Acolyte of Chayula
summary: Sceptre minion Acolyte: crossbow grenades through Act 3, then skeletons, Wolf Pack and finally Plague Harvester spectres, with Pain Offering and Despair as buffs. Waking Dream's chaos Remnants and Mind Over Matter on an ES/evasion base.
gear: Sceptre with +minion levels (also on helmet and amulet); Alpha's Howl for Spirit and presence, Bones of Ullr for more minions, belt with melee splash. ES/evasion armour and capped resistances.
strengths: Very high damage once spectres are online
Tanky from the Mid setup on
weaknesses: Guide author marks it not recommended for HC
Squishy until the Mid setup
Non-minion leveling through Act 3
Spectre capture/upkeep adds friction

name: Grim Pillars Totem Oracle
summary: Spell Totems spam Grim Pillars ice crystals that you detonate with Entangle while Mana Tempest and Elemental Weakness boost the damage. The most-played Oracle on the HC Forbidden Rites ladder: totems do the work while you stay at range.
gear: Wand + Sceptre (Purity sceptre for aura tech) or staff; stack +spell skill levels, life/ES hybrid, capped resistances and chaos resistance. Late game many swap to Chaos Inoculation with ~5k+ ES.
strengths: Totems tank and deal damage while you stay back
Excellent clear and good bossing on low budget
No build-enabling uniques; top HC Oracle pick
weaknesses: Totem placement downtime when repositioning
Heavy visual clutter can hide on-death effects
Chaos resistance must be fixed on gear
CI transition is a risky gear threshold in HC

name: Plant Thunderstorm Oracle
summary: Entangle and Thrashing Vines plant fields that Thunderstorm, auto-cast through Cast on Critical with Forced Outcome, drenches and detonates. Auto-targeting, Blind-applying clear with Wildsurge Incantation scaling plant and storm spells.
gear: Staff or wand/focus with +spell skill levels above all else; life, armour/ES hybrid, cast speed, capped resistances. Nightscale gloves are a popular HC pick.
strengths: Entangle available at level 1 and used all game
Auto-targeting map clear with Blind on enemies
weaknesses: Pinnacle bosses need real investment
Visual clutter
Mana-hungry; Thunderstorm gem level must be tuned for Cast on Critical
Chaos resistance is mandatory, ES does not cover it

name: Frostbolt Comet Oracle
summary: Forced Outcome makes every hit a crit, so Frostbolt (forking via Snakepit) clears while Cast on Critical rains Comets for single target. Freezes nearly everything; goes Chaos Inoculation energy shield at endgame.
gear: Wand + focus or staff with +cold/spell levels and cast speed; Snakepit ring in the left slot from level 32. Hybrid life/ES early, then 5-6k ES before switching to Chaos Inoculation.
strengths: Very high single target through Comet
Simple play once Frostbolt and Snakepit are online
weaknesses: Awkward campaign before Frostbolt/Snakepit; relies on infusion remnants
CI swap is a dangerous transition in hardcore
Pure ES dies fast to burst if recharge is interrupted
Freeze-immune bosses remove a defensive layer

name: Lunar Assault Werewolf Oracle
summary: Werewolf melee that freezes packs with Lunar Assault and shreds frozen targets, with Forced Outcome guaranteeing crits. Life/armour hybrid with leech and recoup, using Entwined Realities to grab nodes around keystones.
gear: Talisman with physical/elemental damage and attack speed; Cloak of Flame + Goregirdle for armour vs elemental hits, capped resistances, life leech on rings/gloves.
strengths: Freeze locks down packs and many rares
Good life recovery via leech and recoup
weaknesses: Melee range in hardcore exposes you to on-death and boss slams
Buff and rotation management is demanding
Attribute requirements awkward for Oracle
Best versions need expensive uniques

name: Walking Calamity Bear Shaman
summary: Bear-form slam build where Furious Wellspring keeps Rage topped up so Walking Calamity constantly rains meteors while Rampage carries you through maps. Armour plus physical-to-elemental conversion and Reactive Growth make it the most common HC Shaman.
gear: Talisman with high physical damage, % physical, added elemental and attack speed, upgraded every ~10 levels. Max armour on all slots, Cloak of Flame + Goregirdle conversion, then 'armour also applies to elemental' suffixes.
strengths: Meteors kill packs while you simply move
Strong layered mitigation: armour, conversion, Reactive Growth
weaknesses: Still melee: big boss slams and on-death effects hit hard
Chaos resistance has no passive tree source
Best defence needs Cloak of Flame + Goregirdle
Single target is moderate without Molten Crash

name: Demon Molten Crash Bear Shaman
summary: Damage-focused bear that uses the Fury of the King talisman to unlock Molten Crash, layering fissure leaps over Walking Calamity meteors. Crown of Eyes and Lord of the Wilds turn Rage-scaled spell damage into huge attack hits.
gear: Fury of the King talisman plus a non-unique sceptre via Lord of the Wilds (needs Spirit); Crown of Eyes helmet. Hybrid life/ES/armour, capped elemental and chaos resistance.
strengths: Top-tier damage for clear and pinnacle bosses
Walking Calamity adds free passive damage
Strong elemental mitigation from Reactive Growth/Avatar of Evolution
weaknesses: Guide author explicitly advises against hardcore: some boss attacks one-shot
Reported stunlock bugs on bosses
Needs expensive uniques to come online
Complex weapon-swap and Rage management

name: Minion Army Shaman
summary: Sacred Flow's Spirit from empty charm slots funds a full army of Powered Zealot spectres and skeletons, buffed by Pain Offering and curses. Energy shield with Chaos Inoculation plus Reactive Growth makes it one of the tankiest Druid setups.
gear: Sceptre with +minion levels and Spirit plus an ES shield/focus; Bones of Ullr boots, +minion-level amulet. Stack 5-6k ES before Chaos Inoculation; charm slots stay empty for Sacred Flow.
strengths: Very tanky: CI energy shield, block, Reactive Growth
Minions take aggro so you can stay at range
Low button pressure once set up
weaknesses: Empty charm slots mean no charm answer to freeze/ailments
Minion deaths in big hits can stall damage
CI transition is a risky gear threshold
Spectre capture and Spirit budget take setup

name: Spark Totem Shaman
summary: Ancestral Bond Spell Totems spam Spark empowered by Archmage, with Sacred Flow supplying the Spirit for the whole setup. A ranged, SSF-friendly caster that keeps distance from danger.
gear: Wand/sceptre + focus with +spell levels and mana; large mana pool for Archmage, ES/life hybrid, capped resistances. Idol of Uldurn and Dream Fragments are strong upgrades but optional.
strengths: Sacred Flow solves Spirit for Archmage and totems
weaknesses: Totem playstyle only from ~level 55; campaign uses Essence Drain
Mana-hungry; Eldritch Battery/mana stacking needs care
Projectile damage can feel inconsistent on single bosses

name: Stampede Slam Titan
summary: Two-handed mace slammer that clears by Stampeding through packs while Earthbreaker aftershocks and Herald of Ash chain the explosions, then bursts bosses with Forge Hammer, Infernal Cry and Hammer of the Gods. Shattering Blow breaks armour on every heavy stun.
gear: Any high-physical two-handed mace plus heavy-armour pieces with life, resistances and 'armour also applies to elemental damage'; no unique is required (For Utopia and Sanguis Heroum charms are upgrades).
weaknesses: Melee range: ground effects hurt
Bosses need a Forge Hammer/cry combo
Slower than ranged builds

name: Strength-Stacking Earthquake Titan
summary: Stacks Strength into Earthquake slams whose Titan-boosted aftershocks (Earthbreaker, Ancestral Empowerment) erupt across the screen, with Hammer of the Gods and Forge Hammer for bosses. Budget route uses Facebreaker; the mirror-tier version runs Reverie and Nightfall.
gear: Facebreaker gloves turn stacked Strength into unarmed damage; pair with Titanrot Cataphract, Defiance of Destiny and a 'fewer enemies to be surrounded' Constricting Command, and fill the rest with Strength, life and resistances. jonno_poe's endgame swaps to a Reverie/Nightfall mirror-tier setup.
weaknesses: Armour is the only real defensive layer
Visual clutter hides ground effects
Core uniques gate the build

name: Brutus Strength-Stack Titan
summary: Dual-wields Brutus' Lead Sprinkler and stacks Strength so every Mace Strike rains Molten Shower fire projectiles, while Stone Skin, Mysterious Lineage and armour stacking make it extremely hard to kill. Levels as a Shield Wall Titan until the maces are affordable.
gear: Two Brutus' Lead Sprinkler maces (dual-wielding doubles the Molten Shower projectiles), a high-armour Warlord Cuirass and Strength on every slot; Constricting Command and charm uniques are late upgrades.
weaknesses: Needs two Brutus maces
Not SSF-friendly
Gear-gated before maps

name: Spear & Shield Bleed Titan
summary: Spear-and-shield Titan that dashes through packs with Rake while Herald of Blood chains bleed/poison explosions, then one- or two-shots pinnacle bosses with Nebuloch-crit Shield Wall bleeds detonated by Fortifying Cry. Crimson Assault aggravates every bleed.
gear: A high-physical spear (socket Soul Core of Opiloti for bleed magnitude) plus a high-armour shield, The Brass Dome and a 'fewer enemies to be surrounded' Constricting Command; Nebuloch on the second weapon set makes Shield Wall always crit.
strengths: Rake doubles as a travel skill
weaknesses: Rake can get stuck on terrain
Clear relies on corpses (weak in Delirium)
Chaos damage is a soft spot

name: Spin-to-Win Quarterstaff Titan
summary: Pure physical quarterstaff Titan that spins through packs with Whirling Assault, heavy-stunning and armour-breaking everything (Crushing Impacts), with Tempest Bell for bosses. A cheap, one-button 'Cyclone at home' rather than a min-maxed meta pick.
gear: Any physical quarterstaff (Sculpted Suffering is a cheap levelling option) with an armour/life chest such as Warlord Cuirass; The Surrender is optional. Mana Leech on the spin helps sustain.
strengths: Heavy stun plus armour break lock
weaknesses: Comes online only around Act 3
Attribute juggling
Low ceiling versus meta Titans

name: Earthshatter Block Warbringer
summary: Mace-and-shield Earthshatter whose spikes are shattered by cooldown-free Infernal Cry (Warcaller's Bellow) for screen-wide clear. The endgame swaps to Brutus Strength-stacking with Renly's Training and Turtle Charm for up to 94% block.
gear: Starts with any one-handed mace and high-armour shield (budget variant cleared T15 on 1-3 Exalted gear). Endgame: Brutus' Lead Sprinkler, Svalinn, Constricting Command (Defy lets skills run at 0 mana), Titanrot Cataphract and Astramentis for Strength.
weaknesses: Can feel squishy before block is built
Endgame block needs pricey uniques
Mana issues until Constricting Command

name: Corrupting Cry Warbringer
summary: Screams enemies to death: Fortifying Cry with Paquate's Pact spreads Corrupted Blood while Warcaller's Bellow removes cry cooldowns and explodes corpses. Giant's Blood two-handed mace plus shield, Renly's Training and Turtle Charm give capped block, and Primal Hunger fuels the rage-regen loop.
gear: A crafted two-handed mace with the lowest Strength requirement you can find (Anvil Maul) plus a high-armour shield; Undying Hate (enables Vaal Pact safely) and Prism of Belief are optional late upgrades.
strengths: Cheap to start, easy to gear
weaknesses: Slow clear
Top-end upgrades get expensive
Monster life regen can stall DoT

name: Chaos Caster Smith (EDC)
summary: HC SSF chaos caster: Essence Drain, Contagion and Chaos Bolt (Withered wand) feed Dark Effigy totems under Despair, while Smith body-armour notables add regen, crit immunity and ailment immunity. Swaps a focus for damage and a shield for safety.
gear: Withered wand with +chaos spell levels and cast speed, a +2 spell focus for bosses and Oaksworn shield for mapping; stack life regen, energy shield and capped resistances. Endgame damage comes from the Hayoxis' Fulmination or Doedre's Undoing uniques farmed in Atziri's Temple.
strengths: Immune to bleed, poison and ignite from Act 3
weaknesses: Slow ramp-up clear
Mana-hungry at high gem levels
Needs Temple uniques for pinnacles

name: Bleed Earthquake Smith
summary: Earthquake and Hammer of the Gods stack bleed and poison while Herald of Blood chains explosions, Shockwave Totems break armour and Smith's Masterwork body armour adds regen, ailment immunity and armour against everything. Minimal-gear starter that is very tanky.
gear: Giant's Blood two-handed mace with a high-armour shield and a Normal-rarity body armour for Smith's Masterwork; Constricting Command is the main upgrade, otherwise stack Strength, armour and resistances.
weaknesses: Clunky and slow
Mediocre clear
Damage is good, not great

name: Ancestral Totem Smith
summary: Ancestral Bond doubles the totem limit so a wall of Ancestral Warrior Totems repeat Sunder while the Smith swings a Giant's Blood two-hander behind them. Forge Hammer, Armour Breaker and Infernal Cry handle bosses; Smith body-armour notables cover defences.
gear: Giant's Blood two-handed mace (weapon damage drives the totems) with a high-armour shield and a Normal body armour for Smith's Masterwork; Alpha's Howl is the only unique in the guide.
weaknesses: Totem placement slows mapping
Runes of Aldur (0.5.0) guide
Gem-hungry setup

name: Spiral Volley Deadeye
summary: Physical bow build that uses the Resonance keystone to turn Endurance Charges into Frenzy Charges, then spends them on Spiral Volley for one-click full-screen clears. Lightning Rods set off by Lightning Arrow, Barrage and Tornado Shot handle bosses.
gear: A high physical-damage bow is everything; Serpent's Egg makes charge generation reliable. Hybrid evasion/energy shield armour with capped resistances, then Maligaro's Virtuosity once you switch to crit.
strengths: Can switch to the sprinting Pathfinder version later
weaknesses: Doesn't work without Resonance and steady charge generation (awkward on low gear)
Struggles with armoured or high stun-threshold map mods
Thin defences for hardcore

name: Armour Piercing Rounds Deadeye
summary: Crossbow Deadeye where Mirage Deadeye and Mirage Archer both fire Armour Piercing Rounds, breaking armour so High Velocity Rounds can land huge Riven Armour hits on bosses. Uses armour and life (The Brass Dome) instead of pure evasion, so it is sturdier than most Rangers.
gear: A high physical-damage crossbow, ideally with +projectile levels, does most of the work; wear The Brass Dome and armour/life pieces with capped resistances. Dr3adful's 'without breaking the bank' planner shows it running on mid-budget rares.
strengths: Two mirages keep shooting while you reposition
Riven Armour gives High Velocity Rounds huge single hits on bosses
Armour and life defence instead of fragile evasion
Has a budget version and a zero-to-hero levelling route
weaknesses: Crossbow reloads plus mirage cooldowns make it a rotation build
Mirages need decent placement
Far fewer guides than bow Deadeye

name: Explosive Shot Deadeye
summary: Crossbow grenadier: Explosive Shot sets off Explosive, Gas and Oil Grenades for big fire bursts, while Tailwind and an extra projectile make it one of the fastest Ranger map clearers. Lots of buttons and crossbow reloads, and squishy until geared.
gear: A crossbow with increased physical and flat lightning damage (an extra-bolt mod helps with reloads); aim for a decent life/evasion body armour early. Then resistances, movement speed and projectile levels.
strengths: Very fast clear with chain explosions
High single-target damage from grenade bursts
weaknesses: Crossbow reloads and many buttons
Mana management
Squishy evasion/life defences

name: Armoured Grenade Deadeye
summary: All-grenade Deadeye: Mirage Deadeye spams Explosive Grenade while Cluster, Gas, Oil and Flash Grenades cover the screen. Built on armour, stun defence and life for 70k+ effective HP, which makes it one of the safest Deadeye setups.
gear: Crossbow with flat elemental damage and grenade/projectile levels; armour-based body and gloves (Valako's Vice) with high life and capped resistances. The armour/stun nodes on the tree supply most of the defence.
strengths: About 70k effective HP in the guide setup
Grenades plus Mirage Deadeye give strong area and boss damage
Smooth grenade campaign route (maxroll leveling guide)
weaknesses: Grenade fuse timing takes practice
Slower clear than evasion Explosive Shot
Heavy Strength investment on a Dex class

name: Lightning Spear Deadeye
summary: Spear Deadeye that throws Lightning Spear for screen-wide chaining bolts and stacks Frenzy Charges (Avidity, Thrilling Chase) to spend on Wind Serpent's Fury or Storm Lance against bosses. Few buttons while mapping; the HC endgame setup adds a Rhoa mount and Wind Dancer.
gear: A one-handed spear with high damage and an empty off-hand (Dance with Death), or Sacred Flame for spirit; Kitoko's Current and Serpent's Egg keep Frenzy Charges flowing. Then resistances, life, evasion and lightning ailment magnitude.
strengths: Screen-wide chaining bolts for fast clear
weaknesses: Bossing depends on Frenzy Charge upkeep
Slow boss kills with low crit chance
Evasion/life only, so hardcore needs care

name: Spiral Volley Poison Pathfinder
summary: Sprint-and-shoot poison bow: Spiral Volley with Armour Break and Corrosion spreads poison across the screen, and Running Assault lets you sprint into packs without being heavy-stunned. Toxic Growth, Gas Arrow and Vine Arrow handle bosses.
gear: High physical-damage bow (Slivertongue early, Voltaxic Rift for the hybrid version) and Serpent's Egg; hybrid evasion/energy shield armour, life, resistances and flat damage on jewellery and gloves.
strengths: Immune to slows and can't be heavy-stunned while sprinting
weaknesses: Clunky early campaign; Spiral Volley only comes online later
High attribute requirements
Mana management

name: Run & Gun Poison Crossbow Pathfinder
summary: Crossbow poison stacker: Armour Piercing Rounds and Herald of Plague clear while you keep running, and on bosses Armour Piercing Rounds, then High Velocity Rounds (Riven Armour), then Fragmentation Rounds melts them with doubled poison stacks. The 0.5 version uses pure evasion, deflection and life.
gear: A crafted high physical-damage crossbow, with Rampart Raptor on weapon set 1 just for Fragmentation Rounds; Snakebite gloves for extra poison stacks. Evasion gear plus Blind lets you reach the deflection cap.
strengths: Melts pinnacle bosses with the APR, HVR, Frag Rounds rotation
Pathfinder slow immunity lets you run almost any map mod
Scales from 'alch and go' (1-2M DPS) to 8M+
weaknesses: Can't run poison from the start; level with Permafrost Bolts and swap once you have a good crossbow
Three-skill boss rotation plus weapon swap
Evasion/deflection can't face-tank the hardest juice

name: Decompose Pathfinder (Corpsewade)
summary: Near zero-button build: Corpsewade boots trigger Decompose with every step, turning corpses (and your own Blood Elemental spectres on weapon swap) into poison clouds, while Plague Bearer and Herald of Plague chain the poison. Chaos Inoculation energy shield, evasion and triple curses slow enemies to a crawl.
gear: Corpsewade is mandatory (cheap; add sockets later). Set 2 uses Trenchtimbre with +minion levels for five Blood Elemental spectres; energy shield/evasion gear with capped elemental resistances and lots of spirit (around 440).
strengths: Effectively one button: you walk and things die
Chaos immune with 4k+ energy shield and 70%+ evasion
Triple curses slow enemies to a crawl
weaknesses: Doesn't start until level 58 (Sacrifice); level as poison bow first
Weak single target without gear
Manual weapon swap and spectre respawn timers
Can scale to thousands of divines

name: Skeletal Reaver Pathfinder
summary: Relaxed one-button minion Pathfinder built for Hardcore: Skeletal Reavers and Skeletal Clerics fight for you, and you only refresh Pain Offering about every 10 seconds. Mind Over Matter, evasion and Sustainable Practices' elemental damage reduction keep the Ranger safe.
gear: Queen of the Forest for movement speed from evasion and Bones of Ullr for minion support; otherwise +minion levels, spirit, evasion, mana and capped resistances. A cheap build to gear.
weaknesses: Lower damage ceiling than the bow builds
Minion clear is slower than projectile Rangers
Few guides; levelling route not documented by the creator

name: Incinerate Pathfinder
summary: Off-meta Hardcore caster: Incinerate's flames, burning ground and Volatile Dead clear while Pathfinder's movement and maxed deflection keep you out of trouble. Whispers of Doom adds an extra curse (Elemental Weakness plus Temporal Chains via Blasphemy).
gear: Evasion gear stacked toward the deflection cap, Queen of the Forest for movement speed, Cracklecreep ring for fire spreading; +spell levels and capped resistances. The creator played it on about 50 divines.
strengths: Hardcore-tested in Runes of Aldur HC Trade
Very high movement speed (140%) and max deflection
Burning ground and proliferation clear packs on cheap gear
weaknesses: Off-meta: few guides and no written levelling route
Channelled Incinerate means standing still briefly
Bossing is modest

name: SSF Rhoa Poison Pathfinder
summary: FatbellyWW's SSF-ladder Pathfinder: Plague Bearer plus Slivertongue carry the campaign, then you ride a Rhoa mount and stack Toxic Growth, Poisonburst Arrow and Toxic Domain. Traveller's Wisdom and Sustainable Practices give 70-80% elemental damage reduction.
gear: Get Slivertongue at level 39 and don't Vaal it early (it can be upgraded now). Evasion gear plus Sustainable Practices for elemental damage reduction; take damage from minor passives as attributes come from gear.
strengths: Mounted 1-4 button play with 70-80% elemental damage reduction
Strong for the price; works self-found
weaknesses: Slow Acts 1-2 until Plague Bearer (use grenades)
Poison damage-over-time ramps up
Rhoa riding has its own movement quirks

name: Ice Strike Amazon
summary: Quarterstaff crit melee Amazon that clears with Ice Strike and Tempest Bell and shatters bosses with Shattering Palm and Charged Staff. Endgame Reverie plus Azmeri Brew makes it far tankier than a typical evasion melee.
gear: High-crit cold quarterstaff; campaign through maps on rare evasion gear with Hollow Palm/Resonance trees, then Reverie body armour with Azmeri Brew for the endgame defensive spike. Evasion helmet/gloves/boots for Stalking Panther.
strengths: Strong single target and fast clear
weaknesses: Melee range in hardcore
Endgame tankiness hinges on Reverie
Several skills to juggle on bosses

name: Werewolf Amazon
summary: Talisman werewolf Amazon that freezes with Lunar Assault, then bursts with Shred and Cross Slash, keeping wolf form up with Lunar Blessing. Fast, mobile and crit-scaled by Amazon accuracy nodes, defended by evasion and deflection.
gear: Physical/crit talisman (Spiny/Maji base) with % physical and attack speed; evasion-heavy armour with life and capped resistances, deflection on gear. Lightning damage matters early; Lunar Blessing at level 52 is the big power spike.
